title: Admin Workflows Conversion Studio — turn scripts into verified tasks
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem: our on-call and SRE teams maintain dozens of ad-hoc scripts and prose runbooks in docs/Drive which are slow to execute, often non-idempotent, and lack telemetry. We want a conversion "studio" that ingests common admin artifacts (bash/python snippets, Markdown runbooks, and recorded CLI transcripts) and produces validated, taskified operators that can run in the Admin Workbench with dry-run, RBAC gating, and observability.

Goal: build a lightweight pipeline and UI that lets an engineer: upload a script or paste a runbook, run an automated analysis that infers inputs/outputs and side effects, propose a typed task manifest, run a synthetic dry-run in a sandbox, and publish the verified task to the operator catalog. The output should be safe by default (principle of least privilege), idempotent where possible, and carry correlated telemetry + audit trail.

Scope: prototype CLI + backend conversion API + minimal console surface for reviewers. Include a validator that checks for non-idempotent patterns (unconditional destructive commands), secret exfiltration heuristics, and required RBAC annotations. Integrations: GitHub for PR-based publishing workflow, Confluence/Drive links for provenance, and Ops telemetry for correlating replays with incidents.

Non-goals: replacing full runbook reauthoring or automating complex multi-service remediation flows in v1. We will not execute changes against production without explicit pre-approved gating and canary steps.
acceptance_criteria: Conversion API accepts a bash/python/markdown input and returns a candidate task manifest with inferred inputs and safety annotations.
Studio UI shows side-by-side original artifact, inferred manifest, and a dry-run execution log from sandbox (no external side effects).
Automated validator flags destructive operations and requires a reviewer sign-off before publish.
Published task appears in operator catalog with telemetry hooks, audit metadata, and a GitHub PR linking the generated manifest.
RBAC gating: tasks require one of the pre-approved roles and honor KMS-enforced secret usage patterns.
steps_taken: Feb 10: Kickoff with SRE and Oncall leads (notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Admin+Conversion+Studio).

Feb 12: Prototype converter that parses shell scripts, extracts flags, and emits a simple JSON manifest (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admin-conversion-studio, branch: feat/manifest-parser).
Feb 14: Built sandbox harness using Docker-in-Docker in ephemeral namespace; dry-run executed sample remediations against a fixture cluster (logs attached).
Feb 16: Ran threat-modeling session with security (see doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2b_StudioThreatModel).
Feb 18: Implemented heuristic validator for destructive patterns (rm -rf, psql --drop) and initial idempotency scoring metric.
next_steps: Finish manifest schema v1 and publish JSON Schema to repo (owner: @arjun).
Wire up GitHub PR creator that opens a draft PR containing the generated task + tests and a CHANGELOG entry.
Add console review page: 'Studio -> Candidate Tasks' with reviewer comments and approve/publish controls.
Integrate telemetry: add correlation-id propagation and wire to Ops metrics dashboard (dashboard link below).
Schedule security review signoff and create a checklist for mandatory RBAC annotations before publishing.
comments: 2025-02-11 Lena Park: Initial spec posted; SRE asked for forced-dry-run mode and an escape hatch UX for emergency publishes.
2025-02-13 Miguel Alvarez (Security): Noted requirement for KMS usage and to ban inline plaintext credentials in generated manifests.
2025-02-15 Arjun Mehta: Prototype parser handles 85% of canonical scripts; failing cases logged in GH issue #23 (shebangless scripts, interactive prompts).
2025-02-17 Priya Shah (SRE): Dry-run logs look good. Two examples produced non-idempotent manifests; added step to wrap changes in reversible transactions where possible.
2025-02-19 QA: Added test harness to replay 50 sample runbooks with fixture inputs; 6 flakey cases require manual instrumentation. Created ENG-442212 to triage flaky conversions.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive inference reduces reviewer burden but increases false positives; we biased v1 for safety by requiring explicit reviewer approval for any manifest with idempotency_score < 0.9. Also limiting execution scope in sandbox to avoid credential/secret propagation. Will revisit to enable safe auto-publish for low-risk tasks.
